newsitem.title: USA: Nebraska fed cattle market quiet, no sales - USDA.
newsitem.headline: Nebraska fed cattle market quiet, no sales - USDA.

text.p: Trading on slaughter steers and heifers was at a standstill, USDA said.

Large weekly movement cleaned up showlists and put packer live inventories in good shape. Few bids of mostly $110.00 per cwt on a dressed basis available Thursday. Majority of this week's sales ranged $111.00-$112.00
Live basis sales - Equivalent 3 percent shrink delivered and FOB, some FOB 4 percent shrink. Dressed basis delivered ( paid on hot carcass weights).
Slaughter heifers - No reported sales. Nebraska Feedlot Weekly Summary:
Slaughter steers and heifers on a live basis 1.00 to fully 2.00 higher, but not tested late; dressed basis 2.00 to 3.00 higher, but not tested late.
Most of the week's business transpired Tuesday when near 80,000 cattle traded, leaving showlists well "cleaned up", and packers well fixed for live inventory.

All buyers bid aggressively, prompted by sharply higher boxed beef returns. Very little trade transpired later in week. This week's sales included 8,100 previously contracted or formulated cattle. Confirmed - None Last Week - 3,300 Last Year - 3,500 For week - 99,700 Sm Pd Lst Wk- 97,600 Sm Pd Lst Yr- 64,000
